h: Making Linton Part of a Cambridgeshire Weekend
p: Linton is the kind of zoo you can do at an easy pace, which makes it a nice antidote to a busy week. Wander slowly, read the signs, and pause wherever the animals are doing something interesting. Smaller zoos often give you a better look than the giants, because you're not elbowing your way through crowds, and the kids can come back to a favourite enclosure as many times as they like. A good tip is to ask a keeper which animal is the biggest character, because they always have a story to share.

The village is set on the little River Granta, with a historic church and old houses lining its streets, so it's worth a short wander after your visit. If you want to turn your day into a weekend, you're in a great spot. The Imperial War Museum at Duxford, a short drive west, is one of the most impressive aviation museums in the country, packed with aircraft from the First World War to the jet age. It's a superb pairing for plane-mad kids and grandparents alike.

Closer to Cambridge, Wandlebury Country Park sits on the Gog Magog Hills with woodland walks and the remains of an Iron Age hill fort, a lovely spot for a run around and some fresh air. Cambridge itself has free museums such as the Fitzwilliam and the Museum of Zoology, which pairs rather nicely with a day at the zoo, plus green spaces like Jesus Green and Midsummer Common for picnics on a sunny afternoon.
